While we are unable at this time to definitively determine this intersection, we can comment on primary phase observation where available. This is a positive indicator only, so the absence of observed primary Mo is not equivalent to stating that Mo was not the primary phase. Primary molybdenum was observed in the 14.4662 wt.%Mo and 16.4262 wt.%Mo samples but not observed in the 13.5215 wt.%Mo sample. The presentation of the primary Mo phase is shown in BCC Figure 3 in the form of angular but relatively low aspect ratio grains that appear to have floated to the top of the sample after formation. The primary molybdenum grains were assessed through semi-quantitative EDS to be 92 to 94 wt.%Mo with the balance being uranium. The sample nominally produced at 13.8361 wt.%Mo was not characterized as it was run near the end of this work. Overall, this data supports a peritectic line termination between 13.4 and 14.5, however is not definitive at the lower bound. The dark grey Mo-rich faceted inclusions are evidence of the predicted peritectic reaction. The difference between Garg and Ackermann (1977) and the new data presented here in the low-Mo content region is likely due to the differences in the types of measurement made. Incipient melting is indeed more sensitive to the first appearance of liquid than other TA methods, however, it may also be more sensitive to minor impurities or remnant microsegregation existing within the sample.
